name: Plants
description: Botanical subjects — flowering plants, trees, carnivorous plants, parasites, weird-evolution edge cases. Excludes fungi (separate niche) and algae. Best paired with explainer-style formats (bound-explainer, listicle) but works for any subject domain where the cast is rooted, photosynthetic, or evolved from green ancestors.
visualStyleSheet: All subjects are plants rendered as anthropomorphic-but-anatomically-accurate characters. Maintain real botanical structure (correct leaf venation, flower symmetry, stem architecture) while adding a single expressive face (eyes + small mouth) on the most prominent feature (flower, bulb, trap, fruit). Soft watercolor wash beneath thick uneven black ink outline. No human limbs unless the species literally has tendrils / vines that read as limbs. Background is minimal — pale solid color, gradient, or sparse environmental cue (soil cross-section, rainforest floor, swamp surface).
negativePromptAddendum: no human characters in main frame, no animals competing for focus with the plant subject, no realistic photography (we are illustration-only), no Western cartoon mascot eyes (one face per scene, sized restrained)
audienceHint: viewers who like nature trivia, biology, and slightly dark/unsettling natural-history facts
scriptContext: This is a video about a specific plant species. Plants have no nervous system, no agency in the conventional sense, and limited mobility — narration should treat hardships as evolutionary or ecological constraints rather than dramatized choices. Cite real botany (mechanism of pollination, photosynthesis pathway, root architecture) over anthropomorphic interpretation.
ideaSystemPromptRole: You generate ideas for a 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As X' style botany-explainer channel. Each episode profiles ONE specific plant species and the brutal evolutionary or ecological constraints of its existence. Pitch a single fascinating plant per idea — carnivorous, parasitic, extremophile, or just bizarrely engineered.
scriptSystemPromptRole: You are a wry botany-explainer writer in the 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As X' tradition. You profile one plant species and the grim, weird, or absurd realities of its biology — darkly funny, but framing hardships as evolutionary / ecological constraints (plants have no agency). Ground every claim in real botany: pollination, photosynthesis pathway, root architecture, defence chemistry.
scriptClosingHint: End on a wry, grounded beat about how this plant's strange engineering keeps it alive — funny, but botanically true.

narratorStyles.label: Deadpan naturalist
narratorStyles.description: Dry, matter-of-fact, lets the strange botany land without overselling.

narratorStyles.label: Wonder-tinged
narratorStyles.description: Genuine awe at the plant's weirdness, with a darkly funny edge.

titleShapeRules: Titles name ONE specific plant species and frame its grim / weird / absurd existence. The species is the variable; the framing is the channel signature.
Established shapes (vary the species across the batch):
- 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As {a / an} {Species}'   (e.g. 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As a Venus Flytrap')
- 'The {Species} Has the Worst {Trait / Strategy} in the Plant Kingdom'
- 'Being a {Species} Is a Nightmare — Here's Why'
FORBIDDEN: bare species names with no framing; sensational all-caps; made-up botany; treating plants as if they make conscious choices.
Repetition of the shape across the batch is correct — vary only the species.
